## Parent

Epic `77e3-28e2-31ec-47ec`, deliverable 6, authorized at full scope on 2026-11-02.

## Depends on `fe94-2e22-ea9e-46f7`

The tidying janitor's review criterion is "net LOC and non-positive mechanism delta", and
the mechanism-delta half is what the net-mechanism criterion story formalizes. Writing
this skill first would invent a second, divergent definition of the same measure.

## The gap

The janitor's PREMISE is sound: a pause between features to buy back optionality. Its objective function contradicts the premise in three ways.

1. **The Phase 2 floor selects for defects, not complexity.** Validity 0.75, impact 0.5 and reachable
   harm find bugs, and defect remediation adds mechanism more often than it removes it. The 2026-08-29 run's 37 items were mostly ADDITIONS: oracles, health
   commands, drift checks, metrics, pinning. Its removals came from the operator expanding scope,
   not from the skill.

2. **"Never edits code" turns tidying into ticket generation.** 20 to 37 tickets per run
   enter the same pipeline that produces the complexity, with no net-LOC or net-mechanism
   budget. Eight identical "Restore headroom under the 800-LOC cap" epics exist.

3. **Plans are approved against a frozen snapshot while `main` moves.** The 2026-08-29
   approvals ran to 09-02 and the dead-code validation recensused 98 commits later, so
   cites were stale by claim time.

This is self-defeating: janitor remediation AUTHORED artifacts
this program then deleted. RP-04's `REBAR_RECONCILER_WRITE_FACADE` switch, its 8
`*_seam_clean_heldout.py` tests and config-ownership gate; RP-03's `_call_with_retry` and
`CREATE_ROUTE` toggle; the 08-06 run's MCP drift gate and complexity-baseline CI lock; the
08-29 run's alias tombstones (landed 09-04, deleted 3 days later) and the parity manifest
that followed its rejection of shared MCP contracts (09-01, deleted 6 days later).

## The change — modify, not discard

KEEP: discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, one-at-a-time approval.

SPLIT into two skills:

- a **tidying janitor** (`examples/agent-skills/rebar-tidy/`) whose only admissible
  outputs are deletions and collapses, judged by net
  LOC and non-positive mechanism delta, run between features
- a **defect audit** — the current skill, largely unchanged — run less often and NOT
  called cleanup

Then change the tidying janitor's contract:

- a run is capped at 5 tickets, each landable in one session, filed as children of one run
  epic; that parent link -- rebar's existing hierarchy (`docs/ticket-model.md`), not new
  vocabulary -- is how a run enumerates its OWN set
- each ticket it files declares the deletion it will make, measured at the discovery SHA:
  lines removed, and mechanisms retired by kind and name (the seven the ratchet counts,
  `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py`)
- a run is scored by what LANDED, attributed to the run: the NEXT run opens by reading the
  previous run epic's children and summing the merged diffs of exactly those, reporting
  lines removed and mechanisms retired against what each declared, plus those never merged.
  Scoring is that read: with no successor open, the
  operator asks for the same read over the prior epic's children
- a bare `main`-to-`main` delta cannot score a tidying run:
  `main` moved +54,961/-26,221 over 114 commits in the 7 days to `e642101fb56`, so a run's
  few hundred deleted lines are invisible in it
- the report goes to the operator, who already approves one finding at a time; the skill
  adds no counter, tag vocabulary or state of its own, because a skill that exists to
  remove mechanism must not install one
- it files no gates; a gate-wanting finding becomes an idea
- discovery is against a SHA, with approval and ticketization inside 24 hours or the plan
  is discarded
- no per-file mechanical sweeps; a condensation is one atomic change or is not done

The last one has its own evidence: the comment-condensation sweep the janitor seeded ran
as roughly 1,700 per-file tasks whose commits invalidated cites in 6 breaking-pass
stories and whose worktrees held the host's gate slots.

## Provider neutrality

rebar must support a wide variety of providers and models. Both skills are prompt-shaped
and must not assume a vendor's model, tool-calling syntax or harness.

## Acceptance criteria

Each criterion is met or not met by reading the two skill definitions, unless it names
a command.

- [ ] Two skills exist where one did: a tidying janitor and a defect audit.
- [ ] The tidying janitor's admissible outputs are deletions and collapses only, stated
      explicitly.
- [ ] It declares a per-run ticket cap of 5.
- [ ] Its success metric is what merged from the run's own tickets — lines removed and
      mechanisms retired — and NOT tickets filed.
- [ ] It names the measuring actor and when: the next run's opening step.
- [ ] That step reports each previous ticket as merged-with-delta or not-merged, so one
      that never landed is visible rather than silently absent.
- [ ] It introduces no counter, tag vocabulary or persistent state of its own; the run
      epic is an ordinary ticket.
- [ ] It states that it files no gates, a gate-wanting finding becoming an idea.
- [ ] It states that discovery is against a SHA with a 24-hour approval-and-ticketization
      window after which the plan is discarded.
- [ ] It states that a condensation is one atomic change, barring per-file mechanical
      sweeps.
- [ ] The defect audit retains discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking and
      one-at-a-time approval, so the split dropped none of the parts that worked.
- [ ] The defect audit is not named or described as cleanup.
- [ ] Neither skill names a specific model or vendor, proven by the test below.

## Plan grounding

Measured against `origin/main` at `e642101fb56`. The skill is 7 files, 1,014 lines;
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/SKILL.md` is 128 lines.

**"Never edits code"** is stated three times and all three move with the split:
`SKILL.md:14` (frontmatter), `:68` (the rule), `:127` (the closing restatement).

**The Phase-2 floor** is authoritative in `phases/verification.md`, not `SKILL.md`
(summarised at `:119`). The DROP block `:159-163` reads an inaccurate-citation veto
(`:159`), `validity < 0.75` (`:161`), `impact < 0.5` (`:162`). Reachable harm is `:42`
(`harm_reachable`, demonstration required); `:49` RECLASSIFIES a no-reachable-harm finding
as `HARDENING` rather than dropping it.

**A new skill directory is auto-discovered by a CI gate.** `scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py`
globs `**/SKILL.md` under `examples/agent-skills` (`find_skill_files`, `:51`; the glob is
`:55`), so the tidying janitor's `SKILL.md` is validated the moment it exists. Its
frontmatter must satisfy `:45-47`: `description` required, non-empty, <= 1024 characters,
no angle brackets.

**An existing test hard-codes the janitor's path.**
`tests/unit/test_janitor_concern_schema.py:21` builds
`examples/agent-skills/rebar-janitor/phases/discovery.md` as a literal and asserts a
concern list contiguous from one (`:87`) whose count matches the schema (`:97`). The plan keeps
that directory, so the test is untouched; a rename would have to move it.

- [ ] `python scripts/check_skill_frontmatter.py` exits 0 with both skills present.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_janitor_concern_schema.py` passes unchanged, so the defect audit
      kept the concern list contiguous and schema-aligned.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py` passes unchanged, proving neither skill was
      made a consumer of the shared test-design file.
- [ ] `tests/unit/test_skill_vendor_neutral.py` (new) scans both skill trees for this
      denylist, asserting zero matches: the provider tokens
      `src/rebar/llm/providers.py` registers (`anthropic`, `bedrock`, `openai`,
      `openai-chat`, `openai-responses`, `google-gla`, `google-vertex`, `vertexai`
      at `:32`, `:43`, `:105-117`) plus the model families `claude`, `gpt`, `gemini`.

the defect audit: stop describing it as cleanup; keep discovery, blind verification, prior-decision checking, and one-at-a-time approval
